### CORE-ACC-01: WCAG 2.2 AA

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Interfaces meet WCAG 2.2 level AA (aligned with EN 301 549), with automated checks in CI and manual screen-reader testing per release.

**Why.** European Accessibility Act for covered services; public procurement rules for schools.

**How to improve.** Add axe-core or Pa11y to CI and fix contrast, labels, focus order and keyboard access.

**Sources.** [EAA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj), [WCAG22](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), [EN301549](https://www.etsi.org/standards)

### CORE-ACC-02: No flashing content

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Nothing flashes more than three times per second.

**Why.** WCAG 2.3.1. Photosensitive seizure risk.

**How to improve.** Slow or remove flashing effects; offer a 'reduce motion' setting that respects prefers-reduced-motion.

**Sources.** [WCAG22](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), [EAA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj), [EN301549](https://www.etsi.org/standards)

### CORE-ACC-03: Inclusive design for children with special educational needs

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Adjustable speed and time limits, audio alternatives for text, captions, dyslexia-friendly typography options, and support for switch or keyboard-only play.

**Why.** Accessibility beyond the AA floor is what makes a learning product usable by every child.

**How to improve.** Add a settings panel for speed, audio, captions and font; test with SEN teachers.

**Sources.** [WCAG22](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)

### CORE-AI-01: No emotion recognition on learners

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** The product does not infer emotions of learners from face, voice, posture, typing or other biometric signals.

**Why.** AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) prohibits emotion recognition in education institutions since 2 Feb 2025.

**How to improve.** Remove emotion inference. Use explicit signals (a help button, a self-report mood picker).

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-AI-02: No manipulative AI exploiting age

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** AI features do not use subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques, or exploit age-related vulnerability, to change a child's behaviour in a harmful way.

**Why.** AI Act Art. 5(1)(a)(b).

**How to improve.** Review prompts and reward logic for persuasion targets that serve engagement over learning; document the review.

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-AI-03: AI interaction and AI-generated content are disclosed

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_generative · Detection: mixed · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Children (and teachers) are told, in age-appropriate form, when they interact with AI and when content is AI-generated. Generated media is marked.

**Why.** AI Act Art. 50, applicable from 2 Aug 2026.

**How to improve.** Add a persistent 'AI' label on AI responses and metadata marking on generated images and audio.

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-AI-04: AI inventory and no training on learners' data by default

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_generative, ai_assessment, ai_adaptive · Detection: manifest · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Every AI component is listed (model, provider, purpose, inputs, outputs, oversight). Provider data retention for training is disabled. Learners' data is not used to train or fine-tune models without a DPIA and a lawful basis.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 5 and 35. AI Act Art. 4 (AI literacy) and provider transparency.

**How to improve.** Create docs/ai-inventory.md and switch providers to zero-retention or no-training settings.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-AI-05: Age-appropriate AI output, tested before release

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_generative · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Input and output filters adapted to the target age, red-team tests in the product's languages before release, and post-release monitoring of incidents.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(e)(f) for chatbots and companions. Best practice for any child-facing generative AI.

**How to improve.** Build a red-team prompt set per age band and language; run it in CI on prompt changes.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-AI-06: No AI persona that simulates a relationship

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_generative · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** AI characters are friendly but never claim feelings, friendship, missing the child, or exclusivity, and do not create emotional dependency. Memory of previous chats is off by default unless needed for safety.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 3(5)(c) and 14(1)(a)(b): such a system would be an 'AI companion' in scope, even in an educational product. DFA proposal: right to switch off relationship-simulating chatbots.

**How to improve.** Rewrite the system prompt persona; add tests that reject outputs claiming feelings or friendship.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-AI-07: Human review of decisions about learners

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_assessment, ai_adaptive · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** No grade, level placement, certification or access decision about a learner is taken solely by automated processing. A teacher can see, explain and override it.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 22. AI Act Annex III(3) human oversight requirements from 2 Dec 2027.

**How to improve.** Make automated results provisional until a teacher confirms; show the reasons.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [AIA-OMNIBUS](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/)

### CORE-CNT-01: Asset provenance and licences recorded

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Every image, sound, font and AI-generated asset has a recorded source, licence, author and, for AI assets, the model used.

**Why.** Copyright compliance and AI Act Art. 50 marking of generated content.

**How to improve.** Keep an assets/PROVENANCE.csv and check it in CI.

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### CORE-CNT-02: Age rating self-assessment

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** The product has a documented age-appropriateness assessment covering violence, fear, language, in-app purchases, contact risks and addictive features (PEGI-style descriptors).

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 16 and 17 foresee harmonised age ratings covering monetisation and contact risks.

**How to improve.** Run a PEGI-style self-assessment and publish the resulting age and descriptors.

**Sources.** [PEGI](https://pegi.info), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)

### CORE-COM-01: No advertising or ad tracking SDKs

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** No advertising based on profiling of minors and no ad, attribution or fingerprinting SDKs in products used by minors.

**Why.** DSA Art. 28(2) bans profiling-based ads to minors on online platforms. The DFA proposal extends this to all traders.

**How to improve.** Remove the SDK. If marketing attribution is needed, measure it on the adult-facing website only.

**Sources.** [DSA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-COM-02: Third-party analytics and session recording reviewed

**SHOULD** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Product analytics and session-replay tools are either self-hosted in the EEA or bound by a processor agreement that forbids reuse of data. Session recording is not used on child-facing screens.

**Why.** Many analytics vendors reuse data for their own purposes, which would make them controllers (GDPR Art. 28).

**How to improve.** Prefer self-hosted analytics (e.g. EU-hosted PostHog or Matomo) with IP anonymisation; remove session replay from child screens.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)

### CORE-COM-03: No dark patterns

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: low

**Requirement.** No fake urgency or scarcity, confirmshaming, pre-ticked options, nagging after a choice, obstruction to leave or cancel, fake notifications, or confusing double negatives.

**Why.** DSA Art. 25, UCPD. The DFA proposal blacklists these in all circumstances.

**How to improve.** Rewrite the copy neutrally, remove timers and pre-selected options, make 'no' as easy as 'yes'.

**Sources.** [DSA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj), [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### CORE-COM-04: Purchases are adult-facing only

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Children are never directly exhorted to buy, and any purchase flow is behind an adult gate (guardian or school account), with the price in real currency.

**Why.** UCPD Annex I point 28 (direct exhortation to children). KIDS Act Art. 13 and 14(1)(c).

**How to improve.** Move purchases to a guardian or school portal; remove buy prompts from child screens.

**Sources.** [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### CORE-DAT-01: DPIA before launch

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** A Data Protection Impact Assessment exists before launch when children's data is processed at scale, with new technology (including AI), or for systematic monitoring of learners.

**Why.** Processing of vulnerable data subjects with new technology is high risk under GDPR Art. 35.

**How to improve.** Start a DPIA with templates/dpia-starter.md. If the school or Ministry is controller, provide them the technical input; they sign it.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-02: Controller and processor roles are defined, with processor agreements

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: low

**Requirement.** The manifest states whether the provider acts as controller or processor, and every third party that touches personal data has a data processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28).

**Why.** Without defined roles nobody is accountable for legal basis, DPIA or data subject requests.

**How to improve.** Record `gdpr_role` and `dpa_signed: true` for each third party, or remove the integration.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-03: No transfers outside the EEA without a valid mechanism

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Personal data of minors is hosted in the EEA, or every transfer outside it has a documented transfer mechanism (adequacy decision, SCCs plus transfer impact assessment).

**Why.** GDPR Chapter V.

**How to improve.** Move hosting to an EEA region or record `transfer_mechanism` for the third party.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-04: No personal data in analytics events

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Analytics and telemetry events carry no direct identifiers (name, email, phone, IP address, precise location, free text typed by the child). Use pseudonymous IDs.

**Why.** Data minimisation and purpose limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(c)).

**How to improve.** Replace identifiers with a pseudonymous learner ID and drop free-text fields from events.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-05: Retention periods enforced by code

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Each category of learner data has a retention period, enforced by an automated deletion or anonymisation job, not only by policy text.

**Why.** Storage limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e)).

**How to improve.** Add a scheduled deletion job per data category and list it in cses.yaml `retention`.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-06: Data subject rights are supported by tooling

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Access, rectification, erasure and export of a learner's data can be executed by tooling (admin function or script), and the process is tested.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 15 to 20. Schools as controllers depend on the processor to execute requests.

**How to improve.** Build an admin export and delete function per learner and test it each release.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-07: No real learner data outside production

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Seeds, fixtures, tests, staging databases and prompts sent to development AI tools use synthetic data only.

**Why.** Purpose limitation and security (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(f), Art. 32).

**How to improve.** Use a synthetic data generator (e.g. Faker) and block production dumps in non-production environments.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-08: No biometric identification of minors

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** The product does not process face, voice or fingerprint data to identify children.

**Why.** Biometric data for identification is special category data (GDPR Art. 9). Disproportionate in education.

**How to improve.** Remove face or voice recognition. Use class codes, picture passwords or teacher-managed login.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-09: Geolocation off and not collected unless essential

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Precise geolocation is not collected. If a feature truly needs it, it is off by default and turned off again at the end of the session.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 11(1)(a) and 11(2) (applied to games via Art. 15(1)(b)). DSA Art. 28 guidelines on safe defaults.

**How to improve.** Remove location permissions or gate them behind an explicit, session-limited opt-in.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-10: Microphone and camera off by default

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Access to microphone and camera is off by default, requested only at the moment of use for a clear learning purpose, and the recording is not kept longer than needed.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 11(1)(b), applied to games via Art. 15(1)(b).

**How to improve.** Request media permissions just-in-time with a child-friendly explanation; never at start-up.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-DAT-11: Consent for non-essential storage and cookies

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Non-essential cookies and local storage are only set after valid consent, and where consent is the legal basis for minors under the national age of digital consent (13 to 16), a guardian gives it.

**Why.** ePrivacy Art. 5(3) and GDPR Art. 8.

**How to improve.** Keep only strictly necessary storage, or add a guardian-facing consent flow.

**Sources.** [EPRIV](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [EDPB-CONSENT](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-052020-consent-under-regulation-2016679_en)

### CORE-DAT-12: Child-friendly privacy information

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Privacy information exists in a version the target age can understand (very short sentences, icons, audio for non-readers), plus a full version for adults.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 12(1) requires clear language, in particular for information addressed to a child.

**How to improve.** Write a one-screen child version of the privacy notice and test it with children of the target age.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)

### CORE-GOV-01: Product declares its CSES manifest

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: low

**Requirement.** The repository contains a CSES manifest (cses.yaml) declaring profiles, age bands, context of use, GDPR role, features, AI use, third parties and chosen compliance level.

**Why.** Accountability (GDPR Art. 5(2)) requires being able to show what the product does with children's data. The manifest is also what lets the checks select the right rules.

**How to improve.** Copy templates/cses.yaml to the repository root and fill it in with the product owner.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-GOV-02: Legal scope of the EU KIDS Act is assessed and recorded

**SHOULD** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: low

**Requirement.** The manifest records whether the product is in scope of the EU KIDS Act (online game, AI companion, general conversational chatbot, social or video-sharing service) or exempt as a service designed primarily for education and operated by or on behalf of an educational establishment (Art. 2(4)(c)).

**Why.** The same product can be exempt when deployed by a school and in scope when offered directly to families. Teams must know which situation they are in for each channel.

**How to improve.** Fill the `legal_scope.kids_act` field in cses.yaml for each distribution channel.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [KIDS-FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/kids-act)

### CORE-GOV-03: Child rights impact assessment

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** A child rights impact assessment (or a risk review in the sense of the DSA Art. 28 guidelines) is documented, considers the best interests of the child, and involves children, guardians and educators in testing.

**Why.** The DSA guidelines and UN General Comment No. 25 ask providers to weigh all children's rights (protection, participation, provision), not only data protection.

**How to improve.** Extend the DPIA with a child rights section (templates/dpia-starter.md, part C).

**Sources.** [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation), [EUKO](https://www.lse.ac.uk/media-and-communications/research/research-projects/eu-kids-online)

### CORE-SAF-01: Most protective settings by default

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Profiles private, sharing off, contact off, notifications off, recommendations of other users off by default. Defaults are only relaxed after age assurance shows the user is an adult.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 8(1) and 11(1). DSA Art. 28 guidelines.

**How to improve.** Flip the defaults in the settings model and add a test that asserts them.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)

### CORE-SAF-02: Notifications only about the child's own activity, off by default, quiet hours

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: notifications · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Push notifications are off by default, never designed to prompt the child to start or resume use, only relate to the child's own activity or teacher assignments, and respect school time and core sleep hours.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(b) and 11(1)(d), applied to games via Art. 15(1).

**How to improve.** Default the push flag to false, remove re-engagement campaigns, add quiet hours (e.g. 21:00 to 08:00 and school hours).

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### CORE-SAF-03: Natural stopping points, no autoplay or endless feeds

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** No autoplay of the next content and no infinite scroll. Sessions have natural endings and regular interruption moments that let the child decide whether to continue.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(a). DFA proposal gives users the right to switch off autoplay.

**How to improve.** Remove autoplay; end each activity with a clear 'done' screen and an explicit choice to continue.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)

### CORE-SAF-04: Time-awareness tools

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** The product offers break reminders and lets guardians or teachers set a daily time limit, protecting school time (outside class use) and core sleep hours.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 9(3) and 20(4)(a) require time-limited access for social and video services. Best practice for all products.

**How to improve.** Add a session timer with a gentle break screen and a configurable daily limit.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [KIDS-COM](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0680)

### CORE-SAF-05: No contact from strangers

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Features: multiplayer, chat, ugc, social · Detection: mixed · Effort: high

**Requirement.** Nobody outside the child's approved group (class, guardian-approved contacts) can initiate contact, see the child's profile or content, or add the child to a group.

**Why.** DSA Art. 28 and guidelines. KIDS Act Art. 12(1), applied to games via Art. 15(1)(c).

**How to improve.** Scope all interaction to closed groups managed by a teacher or guardian; remove user search and contact suggestions.

**Sources.** [DSA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)

### CORE-SAF-06: Child-friendly reporting and support

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: multiplayer, chat, ugc, social, ai_generative · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Wherever children interact with others or with generated content, a report option is one step away, understandable by the target age, processed with priority, and followed by information on help resources.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 19. DSA Art. 16 and Art. 28 guidelines.

**How to improve.** Add a visible report button, a priority moderation queue and a help screen with national helplines.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)

### CORE-SAF-07: Tools for guardians and teachers that respect the child

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: high

**Requirement.** Guardians (or teachers in school use) can manage settings, time and contacts. The child is told when such tools are active. Controls cannot be bypassed by the child.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 20, applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(d).

**How to improve.** Provide a guardian or teacher panel for settings, time limits and contacts, with an in-app notice to the child.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)

### CORE-SAF-08: Proportionate, privacy-preserving age assurance

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: high

**Requirement.** Where age matters, age assurance is proportionate, uses zero-knowledge solutions such as the EU age verification app, does not store identity documents and only keeps an age signal. Self-declaration alone is not relied on for high-risk features.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 27 and 28. DSA Art. 28 guidelines. EU age verification Recommendation.

**How to improve.** Integrate the EU age verification solution or the EUDI wallet; store only an 'over threshold' flag.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [AVREC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-urges-member-states-rollout-eu-age-verification-app)

### CORE-SAF-09: Children can control and give feedback on what they see

**SHOULD** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: B3 (10-12), B4 (13-15), B5 (16-17) · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Children can adjust settings that affect how they interact and what they are shown, give feedback with lasting effect, and easily return to default settings.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 18.

**How to improve.** Add a simple 'my settings' screen with a 'reset to safe settings' button.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)

### CORE-SAF-10: No social comparison or image-altering features

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** No follower counts, likes on the child's appearance, beauty filters, or features that embellish or idealise the child's image.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 11(3).

**How to improve.** Remove public counters and appearance filters; use avatars instead of photos.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)

### CORE-SEC-01: No secrets in the repository

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** API keys, tokens and passwords are not committed.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 32 (security of processing).

**How to improve.** Rotate the exposed key, move it to a secret manager, and add gitleaks to CI.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-SEC-02: Access control on every store of learner data

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Every table, bucket or collection with learner data enforces access control at the data layer (e.g. row-level security), not only in the client.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 25 and 32. Client-only checks are easily bypassed.

**How to improve.** Enable row-level security with policies scoped to class and role; add a test per table.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-SEC-03: Encryption in transit

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** All network calls use TLS. No plain http endpoints for APIs or assets.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 32.

**How to improve.** Switch the URL to https and enable HSTS.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-SEC-04: No personal data in logs

**SHOULD** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Application logs contain pseudonymous IDs only, with short retention.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 32. Logs are often copied to third-party tools.

**How to improve.** Log the learner ID instead of names or emails; add a log scrubber.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### CORE-SEC-05: Vulnerability handling and breach response

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manifest · Effort: low

**Requirement.** A published way to report vulnerabilities (SECURITY.md or security.txt), a process to fix them, and a breach procedure that lets controllers meet the 72-hour notification deadline.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 33. Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations for products with digital elements.

**How to improve.** Add SECURITY.md and an incident runbook with contact chain and timelines.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [CRA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2847/oj)

### CORE-SEC-06: Strong authentication for adults, simple safe login for children

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Teacher and admin accounts use MFA. Children use age-appropriate login (class code, picture password, teacher reset) without email or phone collection.

**Why.** Adult accounts hold data on whole classes. Children should not need personal contact details to log in.

**How to improve.** Enforce MFA for staff roles; replace child email login with class codes.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)
